question.text: The nature of oxide $\left(\mathrm{TeO}_2\right)$ and hydride $\left(\mathrm{TeH}_2\right)$ formed by Te , respectively are :

solution.text:
$\mathrm{TeO}_2$ is oxidizing in nature because it can be reduced from +4 oxidation state to lower oxidation state.
$\mathrm{TeH}_2$ due to less bond dissociation energy easily breaks and hence acidic in nature.
